For the applicant: Mr. Rakesh Kumar Chaudhary, Advocate For the respondent: Mr. Mohinder Zharaick, Addl.
A.G. Virender Singh, Judge.

By way of present application, under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as 'CrPC'), applicant-Raman Kumar has sought his release, on bail, during the pendency of trial, in case FIR No.13 of 2023, dated 06.04.2023, registered with Women Police Station Mandi,
District Mandi, H.P., under Sections 363, 376, 2(n)(3) of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC') and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter referred to as 'POCSO Act').
2.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
In the application, the applicant has sought his release on bail during the pendency of the trial,
mainly, on the ground that he has falsely been implicated, in this case, as police could not connect him with the crime, for which, he has been arrested, in this case.
3. According to him, investigation, in the present case, is complete and thereafter, police has submitted the final report, under Section 173(2) CrPC, before the learned trial Court.
Charges have been framed against him and child victim has already been examined.

4. As per the applicant, he is a young man of 27 years of age and no useful purpose would be served by keeping him in the judicial custody, that too, for indefinite period, as, according to him, chances of conclusion of the trial, against him, are not so bright.

sentences.text:
Apart from this, the applicant has given certain undertakings, for which, he is ready to abide by,
in case, he is ordered to be released on bail.
6.
The applicant earlier tried his luck by moving the similar application before the Court of learned Special Judge, POCSO, Mandi, however, his application was dismissed on 05.10.2023.
7. On the basis of the above facts, a prayer has been made to release the applicant on bail, during the pendency of the trial.

8. When put to notice, the police has filed the status report, disclosing therein, that, on 06.04.2023,
the elder sister of the child victim appeared before the police and moved the complaint, mentioning therein, that her younger sister has been enticed away.
8.1 According to the complainant, she is a resident of the address, as mentioned in the complaint.
She further stated that they are four sisters and their parents have expired.
Out of four sisters, two are married and the complainant is doing some private job in Chandigarh.
Her younger sister (child victim) has passed her Class VIII exam and her age is stated to be 15 years.
According to her, on 05.04.2023, some unknown boy had enticed away her on the pretext of marriage.

She has given the mobile number of the child victim and also disclosed that she has made a call from mobile No.+971506772616.
9.
On the basis of the above facts, complainant has mentioned that the said unknown boy had also threatened her.
Hence, she prayed that an appropriate action may be taken.
10. On the basis of these facts, police registered the FIR under Section 363 IPC.
After the registration of FIR, the police machinery swung into motion.

11. During the investigation, on 27.04.2023, a telephonic call has been received from Police Station,
Pathankot Division-II, regarding the fact that child victim, along with Raman Kumar (applicant),
were found at Hoshiarpur.
Thereafter, child victim was sent for medico legal examination to Zonal Hospital, Mandi, where, she refused to undergo medico legal examination.

Her statement under Section 164(5) CrPC was recorded and thereafter, she was again taken to hospital for her medico legal examination.
12.
On 01.05.2023, during the counselling by CWC, child victim disclosed that she has been raped by the applicant, upon which, she was medico legally examined and the physical evidence were collected.
Consequently, provisions of Section 363(2)(n)(3) of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act were added.
13. On 02.05.2023, child victim was again produced before the Court for recording her statement under Section 164 CrPC.
Not only this, on the identification of the child victim, the spot map of the house, from where, she was taken away by accused, was also prepared.

sentences.text: After completion of the investigation, police has submitted the report against the accused.

Police has also put forward the criminal history of the applicant, by mentioning the details of the cases,
registered against him, which are reproduced as under:-
i. FIR No.19 of 2023 dated 28.01.2023 under Sections 307, 506, 34 IPC.
ii.
FIR No.69 of 2019 dated 19.08.2019 under Section 307, 323, 148, 149, 302 IPC.
iii. FIR No.78 of 2021 dated 02.05.2021 under Sections 323, 324, 148, 149 IPC.
These cases are found to have been registered against the applicant at Police Station Hoshiarpur.

15. Apart from this, according to the status report, FIR No.59 of 2023 dated 24.07.2023 under Section 22-61-85 of the NDPS Act and Section 25-54-59 of the Arms Act, was also found to be registered against the applicant with Police Station Pathankot Division-II.
16. These facts have been highlighted to show that in case, the applicant is ordered to be released on bail, he may not be available for the trial.

Apart from this, another apprehension has also been expressed that in case, the applicant is ordered to be released on bail, he may coerce the child victim,
as well as, witnesses and allure them to depose in his favour.
17. On the basis of above facts, a prayer has been made to dismiss the application.

18. First of all, coming to the criminal cases, which are stated to have been registered against the applicant, admittedly, in none of the cases, the competent Court has inflicted the punishment against him.

Moreover, the registration of a number of cases, under various provisions of Indian Penal Code and other special Acts, does not take away the presumption of innocence, which is still available with the applicant.

19. Secondly, so far as apprehensions, which have been expressed by the police, in the status report,
are concerned, for those apprehensions, reasonable conditions can be imposed, in case, the applicant is ordered to be released on bail.

20. The investigation, in the present case, is complete and this fact is demonstrated from the stand of the police that the report, under Section 173(2) CrPC, has already been submitted in the Court,
against the applicant, upon which, the trial Court has taken the cognizance and charges have been framed against him.

The child victim has been examined, as, the learned counsel for the applicant has also annexed the photocopies of the statements of child victim, as well as, her sister, which were recorded on 05.10.2023.
21.

The chances of conclusion of the trial against the applicant, in near future, are not so bright, as such, no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in judicial custody, that too, for indefinite period.
Moreover, pre-trial punishment is prohibited under the law.

3 cannot be rejected, as a matter of punishment, as the punishment can only be inflicted by the competent Court of law, after the trial.

entities.text: Raman Kumar vs State Of H.P
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 22. Considering all these facts, this Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled for the relief of bail, as claimed in the application, as such, his bail application is allowed.
The applicant is ordered to be released on bail, subject to furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-, with two sureties in the like amount, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court.

24. Any of the observations, made hereinabove, shall not be taken as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case as these observations are confined only to the disposal of the present application.

25. It is made clear that respondent-State is at liberty to move an appropriate application, in case,
any of the bail conditions is found to be violated by the applicant.

26. The Registry is directed to forward a soft copy of the bail order to the Superintendent Jail,
District Jail Bilaspur, H.P., through e-mail, with a direction to enter the date of grant of bail in the e-prison software.

27. In case, the applicant is not released within a period of seven days from the date of grant of bail,
the Superintendent Jail, District Jail Bilaspur, H.P., is directed to inform this fact to the Secretary,
DLSA, Bilaspur.

entities.text: Superintendent Jail, District Jail Bilaspur, H.P.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Superintendent Jail, District Jail Bilaspur, H.P., is further directed that if the applicant fails to furnish the bail bonds, as per the order passed by this Court, within a period of one month from today, then, the said fact be submitted to this Court.
March 16, 2024 ( Virender Singh )
